system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: Row of 4 squares made of matches]

In the figure, 13 matches were used to make 4 squares in a row. What is the number of squares in a row that can be made in this way using 73 matches? Show the calculations that lead to your answer.

Answer: ____

Figure, described in words:
Four squares connected in a single horizontal row, sharing common vertical sides, constructed from 13 matchsticks: 4 horizontal matchsticks along the top (heads pointing right), 4 horizontal matchsticks along the bottom (heads pointing left), and 5 vertical matchsticks dividing and enclosing the squares (heads pointing up).

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Each square added to the row needs 3 more matches (1 new vertical match and 2 new horizontal matches), since the first square needs 4 matches and each additional square shares one side. For n squares in a row, the number of matches is 4 + 3n − ... let us verify: n squares use 2n horizontal matches + (n + 1) vertical matches = 3n + 1. Check: n = 4 gives 3(4) + 1 = 13, which matches the figure. Set 3n + 1 = 73, so 3n = 72, so n = 24. Therefore 24 squares in a row can be made using 73 matches. Calculation: 73 − 1 = 72; 72 ÷ 3 = 24; Answer: 24 squares.
